question: Of the people who open a subscription paywall, how many select a tier and how many finish or abandon checkout, by surface, tier, and billing interval, per namespace and build? Paywall Opened carries source and current_plan. Free Cap Sheet Choice records what a free plan picked on its monthly-cap sheet (source free_cap): upgrade, transcribe_on_phone or dismissed. Upgrade Plan Selected carries plan (tier id), billing_interval, and source. Upgrade Succeeded Attributed carries plan and billing_interval. Upgrade Billing Provider carries provider (play), stage and billing_interval; it is emitted next to the existing purchase events only on the Google Play Billing path, so Play purchases can be told apart. Subscription Plan Changed carries previous_plan, new_plan, billing_interval, and change_source and is emitted from mobile checkout only. The cancel-flow events carry the closed reason enum. The yearly-switch events (monthly to yearly on the same plan) carry surface (home or plans); Failed also carries reason. Upgrade Succeeded and Upgrade Cancelled stay property-less presence events: the registry forbids adding properties to those released ids, so a completed checkout emits Upgrade Succeeded Attributed in the same call. macos_settings_view and windows_settings_view are plan-grid impressions on the settings page, not a blocked purchase gate. Web Checkout opens in a new tab and does not return a cancel URL to this page, so web does not emit Upgrade Cancelled. Upgrade Modal Clicked and Upgrade Modal Dismissed are the app-version update prompt and are not in this funnel. ARPMAU's numerator is the BigQuery plan_revenue_daily snapshot, not these events and not a sum of webhook events. How many purchase-surface presentations, authoritative allowance reaches, visible blocks, upgrade intents, checkout opens, client success navigations, and real restores occur per namespace/build? The eight Subscription-prefixed events use closed dimensions only. Allowance Block Shown counts actual rendered blocks including optimistic local refusal (unknown cause), independently of authoritative Allowance Reached. Legacy checkout resolution is preserved and cannot alone certify new completion telemetry. Paywall Viewed is once per presentation, Upgrade Tapped is CTA intent, Checkout Opened requires an actual checkout page/window, and Checkout Completed is configured-origin/exact-path verified success navigation ONLY, never accepted payment, entitlement or revenue. Upgrade-in-place and reactivation are not checkout completion. Cancellation, dismissal and load/request failures never complete; entitlement refresh or focus cannot manufacture completion. An observed success navigation may precede entitlement-refresh lag. Web Checkout Completed is deferred to SCA-4433. External-browser native chat checkout has no completion return signal. Use authoritative server billing/invoice truth and its paid/trial classification. Billing Subscription Started is a lifecycle signal, not by itself proof of a charge. Restore is server refresh on Flutter only and must classify the fresh read/error, never stale paid state. Legacy Paywall Opened, Upgrade Plan Selected, Upgrade Succeeded and Upgrade Cancelled retain their prior behavior. Upgrade Modal Clicked/Dismissed are not purchase measurements. See contracts/analytics/PURCHASE_EXPOSURE.md for platform boundaries and limits.
zero_policy: Zero new events is expected before this client revision ships. Missing events are unobserved, not evidence of no exposure, cancellation, failed payment or no restore. Web return observation is best-effort and can be unavailable when the opener is isolated, the parent exits or the observer expires. External-browser native chat completion and native store restore are unsupported where no corresponding signal/action exists. Revenue and paid conversion must use authoritative server billing records, not these client observations.
